title: Proper alteration followed by a completely decomposed etale cover
statement: Let $X$ be an integral Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], meaning it admits a finite affine cover by Noetherian rings, with quasi-excellent affine coordinate rings [def-exc-excellent-ring]. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible on $X$ and a finite covering family $(T_b\to X)_b$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations on $\operatorname{alt}/X$ [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. There exist an integral Noetherian scheme $Y$, a proper surjective morphism $f:Y\to X$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose function field extension $k(Y)/k(X)$ is finite of degree prime to $\ell$, and a finite family of separated etale morphisms $v_i:V_i\to Y$ of finite type [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The family is completely decomposed: every $y\in Y$ has a point of some $V_i$ above it with the same residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Each composite $V_i\to X$ factors through a member $T_{b(i)}\to X$. Here $k(Y)$ and $k(X)$ mean the local rings at the respective generic points; the $V_i$ need not be integral. All schemes displayed are of finite type over $X$.

source.place: Expose II, Theorem 3.2.1, printed pp. 29--30; finite affine-open refinement using Corollary 2.2.4, printed p. 27. This is the proper-surjection normal form, not the modification/finite-flat normal form of Theorem 3.2.3.

proof.text: Take the finite rooted refinement tree of [lem-per-alteration-finite-normal-generator-tree]. We prove by induction on the height below a vertex $Z$ that its leaf family is dominated by a proper surjection $H\to Z$ with $H$ integral and generic degree prime to $\ell$, followed by a finite completely decomposed family of separated etale finite-type maps to $H$. All schemes constructed remain of finite type over $X$, hence Noetherian and quasi-excellent by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. A leaf uses $H=Z$ and the identity cover. Before the induction step, Steps 2--8 establish the required interchange for an E-vertex: a finite completely decomposed etale family $E_i\to Z$ with integral sources, followed by integral proper surjections $A_i\to E_i$ of prime-to-$\ell$ generic degrees $n_i$, can be dominated by one proper prime-to-$\ell$ map followed by a finite completely decomposed etale family mapping to the respective $A_i$.

For the interchange, apply [lem-per-integral-etale-chart-flatification] to the finite family $E_i\to Z$ and $A_i\to E_i$. Its hypotheses require integral Noetherian quasi-excellent $Z$, separated finite-type etale integral $E_i$, and proper dominant integral $A_i$ of finite generic degrees: these are precisely the data in Step 1 at an E-vertex. Obtain a normal integral modification $q:Z_0\to Z$, normal integral $E_i^0=E_i\times_ZZ_0$, and integral schemes $B_i$ finite locally free and surjective over $E_i^0$, of ranks $n_i$, with maps $B_i\to A_i$. Here $q$ is an isomorphism over a dense open, so its generic degree is one. Its image is closed and contains that dense open, hence it is surjective. The family $E_i^0\to Z_0$ remains completely decomposed: a residue-preserving lift over the image of $z_0$ gives a point of the fibre product over $z_0$ with residue field $\kappa(z_0)$.

Put $K=k(Z_0)$, $K_i=k(E_i^0)$ and $F_i=k(B_i)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], the generic fibre of an etale chart is a disjoint union of spectra of finite separable fields. Since the source is integral, it has a single generic-fibre point. The generic points of $E_i^0$ lie over the generic point of $Z_0$: an etale map is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and a nonempty open image in an integral scheme is dense. On affine charts the residue-field theorem [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-residue-field-separable] therefore gives finite separable $K_i/K$. The generic fibre of $B_i\to E_i^0$ is $\operatorname{Spec}F_i$: by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] its affine ring embeds in $F_i$; it is a finite-dimensional domain over $K_i$, so multiplication by any nonzero element is surjective and it is a field. Its dimension is the locally free rank $n_i$, hence $[F_i:K_i]=n_i$ is prime to $\ell$. Its characteristic hypothesis holds: $\ell$ is invertible on $X$, hence its image in the $X$-algebra $K$ is a unit, so $\operatorname{char}K\neq\ell$. Apply [lem-per-sylow-simultaneous-field-sections] to obtain one finite $K'/K$ of degree prime to $\ell$ with a $K_i$-embedding $F_i\to M$ for every field factor $M$ of $K_i\otimes_K K'$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, generic fields and quasi-Galois/Sylow argument, printed pp. 29--30

proof.text: Let $N$ be the normalization of $Z_0$ in $K'$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. It is obtained on each nonempty affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Z_0$ by the integral closure $R'$ in $K'$. The ring $R$ is quasi-excellent, hence Nagata by [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata]. The zero-prime case of [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring] and the definition [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] imply that $R'$ is a finite $R$-module. Thus $N\to Z_0$ is finite. The integral-closure theorem [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] identifies $\operatorname{Frac}(R')=K'$ and makes $R'$ a normal domain; [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain] gives normal local rings. The affine normalizations glue by the cited normalization definition. Every chart contains the same dense generic point, so $N$ is normal integral with function field $K'$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, normalization in the Sylow fixed field; Stacks Tags 07QV, 035H and integral closure construction

proof.text: The finite map $N\to Z_0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and surjective because its image is closed and contains the generic point. Its generic degree is $[K':K]$, prime to $\ell$. Composition with $q$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], surjective, and of the same generic degree because $k(Z_0)=k(Z)$. It is of finite type, and $N$ is Noetherian and quasi-excellent by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian, lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability]. These observations supply all hypotheses for the normal-component argument in the next step, without requiring the initial $Z$ itself to be normal.

source.place: II 3.2.1, proper generic-degree conclusion, printed p. 30

proof.text: Set $W_i=E_i^0\times_{Z_0}N$. The maps $W_i\to N$ are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and separated of finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]; their sources are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The normal-component statement [lem-fin-etale-normal-components] decomposes each $W_i$ into finitely many open-and-closed normal integral components $D$. Every such $D$ meets the generic fibre: the etale map is open by [def-weil-etale-morphism, lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], so every nonempty open of $D$ has image meeting the generic point of $N$. The generic fibre is the base change of $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$, namely $\operatorname{Spec}(K_i\otimes_KK')$; by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] it is a disjoint union of field spectra, whose points are exactly the field factors $M$ in Step 3, and each component $D$ has one such function field. The embedding $F_i\to M$ supplies a generic section of $B_i\times_{E_i^0}D\to D$.

source.place: II 3.2.1, the normal etale charts over the finite normalization, printed p. 30

proof.text: The map $B_i\to E_i^0$ is finite locally free, hence finite by [def-pc-finite-locally-free], so the last map is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] (its first assertion applies to every finite map, without a radicial hypothesis). Take the reduced induced closed structure on the closure of the image of its generic section using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. This is an integral scheme $C$; its generic field is $k(D)$ because the section gives a residue-field-isomorphic point over the generic point. The map $C\to D$ is finite, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite, lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition], and birational. Since $D$ is normal integral, [lem-trf-finite-birational-normal-iso] makes $C\to D$ an isomorphism. Its inverse followed by $C\to B_i\times_{E_i^0}D$ extends the generic section, hence gives a map $D\to B_i\to A_i$. The extension uses finiteness and normality; no extension of rational maps by properness alone is asserted.

source.place: II 3.2.1, extension of generic sections; Stacks Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal

proof.text: The components $D\to N$ form a finite completely decomposed etale family. Indeed, for $n\in N$ choose a residue-preserving point $e\in E_i^0$ over its image $z_0$; the compatible maps $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(n)\to E_i^0,N$ yield a point of $W_i$ with residue field exactly $\kappa(n)$, lying on one $D$. The component inclusion is open, so its composite with $W_i\to N$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It is separated and finite type: $W_i$ has those properties, and each component is open and closed, hence quasi-compact in the Noetherian $W_i$. Each $D$ maps to the matching $A_i$ by Step 7. This completes the interchange asserted in Step 1, including finite family, separatedness, finite type and all factorisations.

source.place: II 3.2.1, concluding completely decomposed family, printed p. 30

proof.text: Now perform the induction of Step 1. At a P-vertex $Z$ with child $P\to Z$, apply the induction hypothesis over $P$ to obtain $H\to P$ and its finite completely decomposed etale family. Compose $H\to P\to Z$. Properness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and surjectivity composes. The generic degree is the product of the two prime-to-$\ell$ degrees: if $(a_r)$ is a $k(Z)$-basis of $k(P)$ and $(b_s)$ a $k(P)$-basis of $k(H)$, then $(a_rb_s)_{r,s}$ spans $k(H)$ and is linearly independent by grouping first in the $b_s$ and then in the $a_r$. Thus the product remains prime to $\ell$. The etale family over $H$ and its maps to the leaves are unchanged.

source.place: II 3.2.1, stability under composing proper generators

proof.text: At an E-vertex $Z$ with children $E_i$, the induction hypothesis on each child gives an integral proper prime-to-$\ell$ map $A_i\to E_i$ and a finite completely decomposed separated etale finite-type family $(C_{ij}\to A_i)_j$ mapping to the leaves below $E_i$. Apply Steps 2--8 to $E_i\to Z$ and $A_i\to E_i$. Obtain $N\to Z$ proper prime-to-$\ell$ and a finite completely decomposed separated etale finite-type family $(D_a\to N)_a$ with $D_a\to A_{i(a)}$. Pull back the corresponding $C_{i(a)j}$ to $D_a$, then compose to $N$. These maps are etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], separated finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence, lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. They are completely decomposed: choose a residue-preserving point in $D_a$ above a given $n$, then a residue-preserving point in its pulled-back $C$-family; the two residue-field isomorphisms compose. Every composite factors through the required leaf. The family is finite since both indexing sets are finite. This proves the induction at an E-vertex.

source.place: II 3.2.1, finite-generator induction using the interchange

proof.text: Apply the induction at the root $X$. The tree lemma supplies a map from every leaf to one of the original $T_b$, so composing the factorisations produced above gives $V_i\to T_{b(i)}$ over $X$. Put $Y=H$ in the root's induction conclusion. It is integral Noetherian, the map $Y\to X$ is proper surjective with finite prime-to-$\ell$ generic degree, and the resulting finite separated etale finite-type family is completely decomposed. All schemes were constructed of finite type over $X$. These are exactly the clauses of the item.

proof_origin.place: Expose II, proof of Theorem 3.2.1, printed pp. 29--30; finite-generator preparation in §§1.2--3.1, printed pp. 25--28. Induction and finite-section extension written out using the cited scheme tools.
